points.text: Frozen ground truth vs live-web systems; time-sensitive answers like prices may be wrongly penalized.
+28% headline is absolute points across different splits and driven by abstention.
"Industry solutions" are actually tool-enabled LLM APIs; wording misleading.
"First" multimodal RAG benchmark claim overstated; Table 1 includes WebQA and omits related benchmarks.
"Comprehensive" overclaimed given English-only, single images, 13 domains.
Judge validation headline hides weak Incorrect precision; n and systems unstated; GPT-4o judges GPT-5.
Egocentric property never tested for effect on QA performance; defects confounded with egocentric.
Multi-turn data generated by an evaluated model (Llama-3.2-90B); no removal rates, possible bias.
No limitations section.
No privacy, consent or licence statement.
Claim that multi-turn conversations contain simpler questions asserted without data.
Truthfulness does not equal accuracy minus hallucination in multi-turn rows; averaging unstated.
Task 1 improvement claim reports best case; Table 8 shows it lowers Claude truthfulness.
Inconsistent dataset size and split descriptions (68K entries vs images/entities; split).
"First" claim and comparison table are selective; recent multimodal RAG benchmarks missing.
No related work section; positioning limited to introduction paragraphs.
Criticizes template-generated benchmarks yet uses templates and LLM-generated questions itself.
Claim that prior benchmarks have questions uncommon in real life is unsupported.
Novelty mostly in setting; metrics and design follow CRAG and MT-Bench-101 without contrast.
No result shows egocentric images are harder for MM-RAG; only retrieval recall.
Information dynamism dimension appears only in abstract, never defined.
Single still images vs continuous capture and speech in wearables; scope unstated.
Missing venues in some references.
Table 5 rows should give model versions.
Main text does not stand alone; key procedures and results relegated to appendix.
Analysis of findings is thin with little explanation.
"New challenges" not shown; systems not compared on another existing benchmark.
Very short conclusion and no limitations section.
Information dynamism in abstract is never analysed.
"8K conversations" inconsistent with 6.5K + 2K elsewhere.
21% torso-to-tail statement conflicts with balanced popularity buckets.
28% improvement is absolute points computed across splits.
"Industry solutions" are LLM APIs with search tool; abstract unclear.
Multi-turn conversations being simpler is asserted without evidence.
"Dropped by up to X%" values lack stated baseline, absolute/relative meaning and intervals.
Typos and inconsistent labels.
Table 5 rows should name model versions.
No evidence labels are correct: no annotator counts, agreement, audit or removal rates.
KG answer attributes are raw wikitext, so answers may be noisy.
Judge 99.1% headline hides weak Incorrect class; validation set and systems unstated.
Winner vs baseline compares different splits; +28 is absolute and gain mostly abstention.
Industry comparison mixes live web search vs curated corpora; reasoning and decoding settings unstated.
All results single runs without variance or intervals.
Claimed <5% slice margin-of-error does not hold at evaluated slice sizes.
Retrieval corpus built around the questions; coverage claims reflect construction, not realism.
Web recall estimate of 89% has no described estimation method.
Egocentric effect on QA never shown; confounded with image defects.
Thresholds and budgets have no stated selection split.
Multi-turn truthfulness differs from accuracy minus hallucination; averaging unstated.
Inconsistent counts (8K vs 8,418; 68K entries) and appendix numbering.
Information dynamism mentioned in abstract only; never defined or analysed.
21% torso-to-tail conflicts with equal-bucket construction.
15% low-quality egocentric image figure miscomputed.
Privacy, consent, de-identification and image licensing for daily-life data not addressed.
No latency, token cost or answer length reported for deployment relevance.
Single still images, no speech or non-English; out-of-scope not stated.
Realism untested: questions not from real users, US-centric examples, no user study.
No risk-coverage analysis to show whether winners' lower hallucination is just abstention.
Corpus recall should be estimated with pooled relevance judgments.
Product examples cited without evidence benchmark reflects them.
Missing details of dataset creation and question quality assurance (annotators, agreement, bias).
Auto-evaluator validation lacks methodological transparency.
Low benchmark retriever recall bounds performance; cannot disentangle retrieval from reasoning.
Unclear whether RAG, search-augmented or long-context benchmark given fixed search API.
Unclear whether benchmark targets wearable use or comprehensive scenarios.
Need more dataset details: question distribution, intention, examples.
Semi-synthetic/LLM-generated questions; difference from real human queries unclear.
Low image-search recall biases experiments; visual entity recognition conclusion questionable, encoder maybe weak.
Prompts to evaluated models not described.
Metric definitions unclear: incorrect vs hallucination, negative truthfulness computation.
Unclear whether multi-turn search avoids returning same content.
Experiments and analyses need strengthening.
No significant analysis or interesting insights from benchmark.
No methodology proposed to improve model capabilities.
Truthfulness = Accuracy - Hallucination not consistent in paper.
Privacy and bystander identifiability risks; anonymization and consent undocumented.

P.summary: Frozen ground truth penalizes time-sensitive answers of live-web systems.
28% headline gain is absolute, cross-split and driven by abstention.
Industry solutions are tool-enabled APIs; comparison settings unclear and mismatched.
"First" claim overstated; comparison table selective.
Scope limits (single images, English-only, no speech) unstated; comprehensive overclaimed.
Judge validation headline hides weak class; set and per-system validity unstated.
Egocentric effect on QA never tested; confounded with defects.
Multi-turn data generated by an evaluated model; possible bias.
No limitations section.
Privacy, consent and licensing unaddressed.
Multi-turn questions simpler claim unsupported.
Truthfulness inconsistent with accuracy minus hallucination.
Task 1 improvement claim cherry-picks best case.
Inconsistent dataset size numbers.
No related work section.
Inconsistent critique of templates while using template/LLM questions.
Unsupported claim that prior benchmark questions are unnatural.
Novelty relative to CRAG and MT-Bench-101 unclear.
Information dynamism claimed but never defined or analysed.
Reference venues missing.
Model versions missing in Table 5.
Main text not self-contained; key content in appendix.
Analysis of findings thin.
New challenges not shown against existing benchmarks.
Torso-to-tail percentage conflicts with balanced buckets.
Reported drop percentages lack baseline definition and intervals.
Typos.
Label correctness unverified; annotation process undocumented.
KG answers contain raw wikitext noise.
No variance or confidence intervals.
Slice margin-of-error claim invalid at slice sizes.
Retrieval corpus built around questions; realism overstated.
Web corpus recall estimate method undescribed.
Hyperparameter selection split unstated.
Low-quality egocentric percentage miscomputed.
No latency or cost reporting.
Question realism untested versus real user queries.
Product examples unsupported.

Q.summary: Dataset creation and question quality-control details missing.
Low retriever recall bounds performance and confounds conclusions.
Benchmark type unclear: RAG vs search-augmented vs long-context.
Question distribution, intention and examples underdescribed.
Synthetic questions vs real human queries.
Metric definitions and truthfulness computation unclear/inconsistent.
